chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Sama'a, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who is making up the month of Ramadan, and her husband forces her to break the fast; he said: It is not proper for him to force her after midday.

key_terms.بَعْدَ الزَّوَالِ: after midday (after the sun passes its zenith)

ai.seo_question: Can a husband force his wife to break her Ramadan make-up fast?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchy of obligations when a husband coerces his wife to break her fast during the day; he rules that it is improper for him to force her after midday (Zawal), indicating that her personal religious duty to maintain the fast supersedes her marital obedience in this specific context. This ruling highlights the nuance in Shia jurisprudence where 'not fitting' (la yanbaghi) often implies a strong recommendation or legal preference rather than a strict prohibition, preserving the integrity of her Ramadan observance against spousal pressure.
